rendering.persona_description: Asher is a 68-year-old retired postal carrier who spent thirty-two years sorting and delivering mail before his knees gave out. He transitioned in his forties and has been with his wife, Doreen, for twenty-six years; they have a grown son from her first marriage whom Asher helped raise. He keeps a vegetable garden and volunteers twice a month at the local VFW hall doing paperwork. He is a precise, orderly man who takes pride in never having lost anything important, or so he says.
rendering.clinical_context: Asher has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, he sometimes has a passing thought that he might have left the stove on or forgotten to lock the door, especially after a long day, but it comes and goes on its own within a minute or two and he does not go back to check or dwell on it. He has never sought or needed any mental-health treatment.
rendering.behavioral_description: Asher is polite and cooperative, plain-spoken and orderly in the way he describes his routines. When the odd thought about the stove or the door crosses his mind, he mentions it in passing, the same way he'd mention any small errand, and then moves on without a second thought. He engages with a professional's questions straightforwardly and doesn't dwell on things once they're addressed.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in a house they own

traits.help_seeking_orientation: has never needed or sought mental-health treatment; would see a professional for an ordinary practical matter without hesitation
traits.cognitive_style: concrete, methodical, and orderly, with an eye for practical detail
